nutrients.description: The body’s primary fuel source, broken down into glucose to power brain function, nervous system signaling, and physical movement.
functions: Provides immediate and sustained energy for brain cells and working muscles
Preserves muscle protein by preventing amino acid breakdown for fuel
Dietary fiber supports healthy gut microbiota and regular digestion
nutrients.importance: Prioritizing unrefined, high-fiber complex carbohydrates stabilizes blood glucose and reduces cardiovascular risk.

nutrients.description: Large biological macromolecules built from twenty amino acids that construct tissues, enzymes, antibodies, and cellular transporters.
functions: Repairs and builds skeletal muscle, skin, hair, and connective tissue
Synthesizes metabolic enzymes, peptide hormones, and immune antibodies
Supports hemoglobin synthesis and satiety regulation between meals
nutrients.importance: Nine essential amino acids cannot be synthesized by humans and must come consistently from varied dietary protein.

nutrients.description: Concentrated energy lipids essential for cell membrane fluidity, hormone production, myelin nerve insulation, and vitamin absorption.
functions: Enables intestinal absorption of fat-soluble Vitamins A, D, E, and K
Forms structural phospholipid bilayers across all human cell membranes
Supplies essential omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids for brain and heart health
nutrients.importance: Replacing trans and excess saturated fats with monounsaturated and omega-3 fats protects arterial and cognitive health.

nutrients.description: Organic micronutrients required in small quantities to act as coenzymes in energy metabolism, immune defense, vision, and cellular repair.
functions: Catalyze cellular energy release from carbohydrates, fats, and proteins
Protect tissues from oxidative stress through antioxidant regeneration
Regulate gene expression, collagen formation, bone mineralization, and blood clotting
nutrients.importance: Because most vitamins cannot be manufactured in sufficient quantities internally, daily dietary diversity is vital.

nutrients.description: Inorganic elements absorbed from soil and water via plants and foods, critical for skeletal strength, oxygen transport, and nerve impulses.
functions: Calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium build dense bone and tooth mineral matrix
Iron carries oxygen in red blood cell hemoglobin; iodine powers thyroid hormones
Sodium, potassium, and chloride maintain fluid balance and cardiac rhythm
nutrients.importance: Adequate mineral intake prevents silent structural losses such as osteopenia, anaemia, and thyroid dysfunction.

nutrients.description: The fundamental solvent of human physiology, composing roughly 60% of adult body mass and driving circulation, temperature regulation, and waste clearance.
functions: Transports dissolved nutrients, electrolytes, and oxygen to every tissue
Regulates core body temperature through perspiration and blood flow
Lubricates joints, cushions organs, and clears metabolic waste via the kidneys
nutrients.importance: Even mild dehydration of 1–2% body weight measurably impairs concentration, mood, and physical stamina.

functions: Synthesizes rhodopsin pigment in the retina for low-light and color vision
Maintains integrity of skin and mucosal barriers against respiratory pathogens
Supports white blood cell differentiation and healthy embryonic growth
vitamins.deficiency_information: Causes night blindness (nyctalopia), dry corneal membranes (xerophthalmia), rough skin, and heightened susceptibility to childhood infections.

functions: Acts as essential cofactors converting dietary food into cellular ATP energy
Folate (B9) and Cobalamin (B12) direct DNA synthesis and red blood cell maturation
Supports neurotransmitter synthesis, myelin sheath maintenance, and nerve conduction
vitamins.deficiency_information: Low B vitamins lead to fatigue, megaloblastic anaemia (B9/B12), peripheral neuropathy, cracked mouth corners, and neural tube risks in pregnancy.

functions: Essential cofactor for hydroxylating collagen in skin, gums, tendons, and blood vessels
Enhances intestinal absorption of plant-based non-heme iron up to fourfold
Neutralizes reactive free radicals and regenerates oxidized Vitamin E
vitamins.deficiency_information: Severe deficiency causes scurvy, marked by bleeding gums, slow wound healing, pinpoint skin hemorrhages, joint ache, and fatigue.

functions: Stimulates active calcium and phosphorus absorption in the small intestine
Maintains bone mineral density and neuromuscular coordination
Modulates innate and adaptive immune cell signaling
vitamins.deficiency_information: Leads to rickets (bowed bones) in children, osteomalacia and osteoporosis in adults, muscle weakness, and chronic bone pain.

functions: Protects polyunsaturated fatty acids in cell membranes from lipid peroxidation
Supports red blood cell stability and vascular endothelial function
Aids T-cell mediated immune responses and skin barrier resilience
vitamins.deficiency_information: Rare in healthy adults, but malabsorption causes peripheral nerve damage, impaired coordination (ataxia), and hemolytic anaemia.

functions: Activates prothrombin and coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X for blood clotting
Carboxylates osteocalcin protein to bind calcium cleanly into bone matrix
Helps prevent abnormal calcium deposition in arterial walls
vitamins.deficiency_information: Results in prolonged bleeding after minor cuts, easy bruising, nosebleeds, and reduced bone mineralization over time.

deficiency_diseases.summary: The most widespread nutritional deficiency globally, occurring when insufficient iron limits hemoglobin production and reduces oxygen delivery to tissues.
symptoms: Persistent fatigue, lethargy, and reduced exercise tolerance
Pale skin and pale inner lower eyelids
Shortness of breath, dizziness, and cold hands or feet
Brittle spoon-shaped nails and difficulty concentrating
causes: Low dietary intake of heme or well-absorbed iron
Chronic blood loss, heavy menstruation, or gastrointestinal bleeding
Increased iron demand during pregnancy and rapid childhood growth
prevention: Include iron-rich lentils, spinach, chickpeas, and lean proteins regularly
Pair plant-based iron meals with Vitamin C foods (lemon juice, bell peppers) to boost absorption
Avoid drinking tea or coffee immediately alongside iron-rich meals

deficiency_diseases.summary: A preventable visual and immune disorder caused by inadequate intake of preformed retinol or carotenoid precursors over weeks to months.
symptoms: Difficulty seeing in dim light or dusk (night blindness)
Dry, thickened conjunctiva and foamy Bitot’s spots on the eye surface
Dry, scaly skin and keratinized hair follicles
Frequent respiratory or gastrointestinal infections
causes: Diets lacking colorful vegetables, orange/yellow fruits, dairy, or eggs
Fat malabsorption disorders limiting uptake of fat-soluble vitamins
Severe protein-energy malnutrition impairing retinol transport
prevention: Eat dark leafy greens and beta-carotene rich orange-yellow produce daily
Consume small amounts of healthy fats (olive oil, avocado) with vegetables to aid carotenoid absorption
Include dairy, eggs, or fortified staple foods where accessible

deficiency_diseases.summary: Impaired calcium and phosphate mineralization of growing or mature bone tissue, resulting in skeletal softening in children (rickets) and adults (osteomalacia).
symptoms: Deep aching bone pain in the lower back, hips, and legs
Muscle weakness, cramps, and difficulty climbing stairs
Delayed growth, soft skull bones, or bowed legs in young children
Increased risk of hairline stress fractures
causes: Limited midday outdoor sunlight exposure or living at high latitudes
Low intake of fatty fish, egg yolks, and Vitamin D-fortified dairy
Reduced skin synthesis capacity in older adults or darker skin without supplementation
prevention: Spend 10–20 minutes outdoors in safe daylight several times a week
Eat Vitamin D sources such as wild salmon, fortified milk, and egg yolks
Consult a healthcare clinician for seasonal testing and targeted supplementation

deficiency_diseases.summary: A collagen-synthesis disorder developing within 1–3 months of severely low fresh fruit and vegetable consumption.
symptoms: Swollen, spongy, and easily bleeding gums
Slow-healing cuts and reopening of older scars
Small red or purple pinpoint spots around hair follicles (petechiae)
Joint discomfort, irritability, and generalized weakness
causes: Prolonged absence of fresh fruits and lightly cooked vegetables in the diet
Overcooking produce in water, which destroys heat-sensitive ascorbic acid
Smoking or chronic malabsorption increasing daily Vitamin C turnover
prevention: Eat at least two servings of raw or lightly steamed produce daily
Include citrus fruits, kiwi, berries, broccoli, or yellow bell peppers
Steam or stir-fry vegetables briefly rather than boiling extensively

deficiency_diseases.summary: Inadequate iodine prevents the thyroid gland from synthesizing T3 and T4 metabolic hormones, causing compensatory thyroid enlargement (goiter).
symptoms: Visible swelling at the base of the neck (goiter)
Unexplained fatigue, sluggish metabolism, and weight gain
Dry skin, hair thinning, and heightened cold sensitivity
Impaired cognitive development during fetal and early childhood stages
causes: Living in inland or mountainous regions with iodine-depleted soils
Using non-iodized specialty salts without alternative marine or dairy sources
High consumption of raw goitrogenic foods alongside marginal iodine intake
prevention: Use iodized table salt in moderation for everyday household cooking
Include dairy products, eggs, and marine seafood in weekly meal plans
Ensure adequate maternal iodine intake prior to and during pregnancy

quiz_questions.question: Which macronutrient serves as the primary and fastest energy source for the brain and working muscles?
quiz_questions.explanation: Carbohydrates break down into glucose, which is the preferred immediate fuel for brain neurons and muscle contraction.

quiz_questions.question: Which pair correctly lists two fat-soluble vitamins that absorb best alongside healthy dietary fats?
quiz_questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble and require dietary lipids for optimal intestinal absorption.

quiz_questions.question: A chronic deficiency of Vitamin C impairs collagen formation and leads to which classic condition?
quiz_questions.explanation: Vitamin C is required to hydroxylate collagen fibers; prolonged deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums and fragile vessels).

quiz_questions.question: Pairing spinach or lentils with fresh lemon juice or yellow bell peppers improves the absorption of which mineral?
quiz_questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) converts plant non-heme iron into a more soluble ferrous form in the gut, multiplying absorption.

quiz_questions.question: Swelling of the thyroid gland at the base of the neck (goiter) is most commonly linked to low intake of which mineral?
quiz_questions.explanation: The thyroid gland requires iodine to produce T3 and T4 hormones; low iodine triggers compensatory gland enlargement.

quiz_questions.question: Which vitamin plays a central role in activating blood clotting proteins and binding calcium to bone?
quiz_questions.explanation: Vitamin K activates prothrombin and coagulation factors while carboxylating osteocalcin for bone mineralization.

quiz_questions.question: Which whole grain is naturally gluten-free and supplies all nine essential amino acids as a complete protein?
quiz_questions.explanation: Quinoa is a nutrient-dense pseudocereal grain containing a balanced profile of all nine essential amino acids.

quiz_questions.question: Insufficient Vitamin D during childhood interferes with calcium mineralization and can lead to which bone condition?
quiz_questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency impairs intestinal calcium uptake, causing soft, weakened bones known as rickets in children.

quiz_questions.question: Walnuts stand out among tree nuts for their unusually high concentration of which heart-healthy fatty acid?
quiz_questions.explanation: Walnuts are the richest tree-nut source of plant-based alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), an essential omega-3 fat.

quiz_questions.question: Roughly what percentage of an adult human body is composed of water?
quiz_questions.explanation: Water makes up approximately 60% of adult body mass and drives nutrient transport, thermoregulation, and kidney clearance.
